Print_Text_ArtemisNote_info:
LIAISON NOTEBOOK - 2nd Battalion, C Company

July 6, 1993. Orders received: seal off Muldraugh. Nobody gets in, nobody gets out. Nobody tells us why.

July 7. Unmarked trucks at night, heading south. Men in white suits. One word stenciled on the crates: ARTEMIS.

July 9. Sarge says we'll be relieved in forty-eight hours. He's lying. He stopped eating.

July 10. One of the suit guys slipped me a piece of paper as he walked by. His hands were shaking.
"If it goes bad, listen to %1. At night. First the numbers, then the voice. Write everything down. - V."

July 11. It went bad.
Print_Text_ArtemisBadge_info:
ACCESS BADGE - OPERATION ARTEMIS

Level 3. March Ridge Detachment.
Cleared for "S" facilities.

Holder: Sergeant R. Halloway.

On the back, in marker: "Rosewood-South. Level -17. Do not lose."
Print_Text_ArtemisMissionOrders_info:
MISSION ORDERS - OPERATION ARTEMIS - SECRET
March Ridge Detachment. Date: July 4, 1993.

1. As soon as the first cases appear in the county, the detachment collects samples from the designated health facilities.
2. Collection point no. 1: West Point clinic. Samples are handed over in person, bypassing local authorities.
3. Results are transmitted through relay station KY-7, between Brandenburg and Riverside.
4. Technical contact: V., Rosewood-South facility.
5. Personnel do not leave the perimeter. No exceptions.

Handwritten in the margin: "Why the 4th? Nobody was sick on the 4th. - H."
Print_Text_ArtemisPatientFile_info:
WEST POINT CLINIC - PATIENT FILE NO. 0

Admitted July 6, 1993, 3:40 AM. Male, about 40, identity unknown.
Fever of 104.9. Confusion, then aggression. Bite on the left forearm, which he calls "nothing".

5:10 AM: restrained. Haloperidol, three doses: no effect.
5:40 AM: Nurse K. Dunn, bitten while restraining him, isolated in exam room 2 at her own request. Door locked.
6:20 AM: the needle bends on the blood draw. Skin and muscle abnormally hard.
7:00 AM: no pulse for four minutes, then activity resumed. Fixed pupils.

Samples: blood, cerebrospinal fluid.
Handed over July 6 at 11 AM to two men from the "federal health service". ARTEMIS badge. They asked for the results to go through the Brandenburg relay station.

Note by Dr M. Okafor: "They were waiting at the door when the patient arrived. They knew."
Added below, in another hand: "He is still wandering the clinic. Sedatives don't stop him; blows barely do."
Print_Text_ArtemisRelayLog_info:
RELAY STATION KY-7 - TRANSMISSION LOG

07/07: encrypted link with Rosewood-South. Order: broadcast sequence 7-1-4-9 every hour. Call sign reserved for extraction.
07/09: traffic doubled. No answer from March Ridge.
07/10: Miller, the technician, ran off into the woods at a sprint. He hadn't slept in three nights. If he comes back, don't let him get close.
07/11: V. came by at night. He recorded a message on the backup tape. He says the machine in the control room will play it as soon as the power comes back.
07/12: grid shutdown announced for tomorrow. I'm leaving V.'s map in the desk drawer. If anyone reads this: get the power back on and turn on the radio in the control room.
Print_Text_ArtemisDossier_info:
ARTEMIS PROGRAM - ROSEWOOD-SOUTH FACILITY - LEVEL -17

Subject: data collection on the Knox agent.

The perimeter is held until a usable sample is obtained. "They need more data."
Origin of the agent: undetermined. Hypotheses noted in the margin: "came from the East"; "escaped".

Evacuation protocol: the bearer of this file has priority.
- Air route: Knox Boundary Camp landing zone, south of Louisville. Call with a military radio, on the operation's frequency, giving call sign 7-1-4-9. Pickup every day at dawn: hold the zone until touchdown.
- River route: the Ohio, under patrol surveillance. West exit through the guarded Esther Kinsella bridge, northeast exit through the Louisville boom; posts lit by floodlights on generators.
- Checkpoint: Clark Memorial Bridge, Louisville. Blood test on entry, quarantine of at most one hour, with or without this file, negative final test required.

Handwritten on the back: "I couldn't get it out myself. Maybe you can. The army walkie-talkie in the cabinet is tuned to our frequency: call them as soon as you're out. By the river: a boat waits at the Riverside pontoon for the west, another at the Louisville docks for the east, the key on the pontoon. Without a boat, my ferryman crosses from Brandenburg, but only if the Kinsella bridge is dark. Wherever you go, look for the green smoke: that's us. - V."
Print_Text_ArtemisBasePlan_info:
ACCESS PLAN - ROSEWOOD-SOUTH FACILITY

Level 0: enter through the east double door. Cross the hall westward to the airlock. The airlock stairs go down to level -13.

Level -13: cross the floor southward to the second stairs.

Level -16: leave the second stairs here (at the bottom, on -17, there is no way to the archives). Follow the corridor north, then east, to the small stairs going back down.

Level -17: follow the corridor north. The archives are at the end, door on the left. Filing cabinets along the wall.

The blast doors open with the access card.

Handwritten: "I left the emergency lights on, but their batteries are running low. Follow the red lights. The sensors go off every night from 23:15 to 1:15; outside those hours, the alarm goes off as soon as you get in, and keeps ringing while you're inside. The file carries a chip: the archive gate will ring when you walk out with it. Then run for the exit. - V."

Recipient: satellite lab, Tikitown (beneath the Proxima office).

Receipt signed: V.

Print_Text_ArtemisLabNotes_info:
SATELLITE LAB - LEVEL -4 - HANDWRITTEN NOTES BY V.

The West Point samples arrived on the 8th. They set up "volunteers" on level -3; the morgue is on -5.
Nobody here is looking for a cure. We measure: speed, contagion, the end.
Everything goes to the base southwest of Rosewood, level -17.

Written at the bottom of the page: "If you read this, go to the base. The sensors are off from 23:15 to 1:15. - V."
